New York City, NY –  Pop girl group, ‘SHe’ will be hosting a "Hook on Love" concert at Tonic Sports Bar & Restaurant in Times Square, New York City on Wednesday, January 30th, 2013, from 8pm til 12am.  "Hook on Love" Concert will allow SHe to fundraise money for the Sandy Hook Elementary  victims’ families and to raise awareness and promote a message to stop gun violence nationally. 

As the nation is still in shock over the tragic loss of 20 children and 6 teachers at Sandy Hook Elementary, 
local artists (SHe, Ethan Kray and Katherine Hernandez) are coming together to raise funds and promote a message to end gun violence.

Tonic Bar & Restaurant will generously donate all door funds from January 25th-30th. In In addition, from now until January 30th, Tonic Bar will be serving specialty drinks, $3 for every $10 specialty drink sold, will go to Sandy Hook School Support Fund c/o Newtown Savings Bank, which is allocating donations and disbursing relief funds to the victims’ families.

In March, Lakota artist Gerald Cournoyer will be traveling to Pittsburgh from the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation in South Dakota where he is an instructor at Oglala College.  During his visit here he plans to host art events at both the Hot Metal Bridge Faith Community and the Wallace Memorial Presbyterian Church in Greentree.  Last summer, both churches took trips to Pine Ridge and Gerald’s visit will continue to strengthen our relationship with the Lakota community there.

Meet Lakota Artist Gerald Cournoyer
Sunday, March 17 @ HMBFC (5pm)
At 5pm Gerald will share his story and show some of his work. 

Dinner will be served at 6pm, 

and then starting at 7pm all creative types are encouraged to show and discuss a piece of their own art.

data.description:
After screaming through the age of industrial worship, progress of the tangible is flattened, our immediate environment comes to a sharp focus. All prey has fallen. We have hunted energy, material, commodity, design, and we shall not be celebratory, as a formidable distance stands gray between the relic and modernity. Debris scattered through the foreground presenting shards, remnants of persistence and pursuit. Protrusions of such infrastructures better serve us now as coordinate beacons and offer a sheltering surveyance.

Over 80 years old, 258 feet tall, and 218 feet wide. A Steel I-beam skeleton skinned with a wide corrugation of riveted steel defines the parameter. An abandoned vessel with no modern facility, the 24-sided polygon (icosikaitetragon) stands vacant. A belly of sludge residue and fumes.

Join us on the 1st floor, B-side of the CopyCat to view new works by Benjamin Kelly. 


http://benjaminkelleystudios.com
http://thetankgallery.org/
data.name: REAP - Work by Benjamin Kelly

data.description:
Hey all,
I recently started freelancing on my own, and I represent a Broadway actress by the name of Adelaide Mestre . She has a fascinating life story as not only the great granddaughter of Marshall Field but as a half Cuban American woman. I would love to have you all come and see the show "Top Drawer", which is Adelaide's one woman, off-Broadway show. It's an amazing production directed by Lauren 'Coco' Cohn of 'Mamma Mia!' fame. 

The show is an autobiographical  journey setting in the Upper East Side of Manhattan and ventures into the old city streets of Cuba on a mission to re-discover her family’s heritage. Adelaide struggles through the issues of having a gay father, and having to cope with his tragic suicide. Dealing with serious issues with a spirit of levity, Adelaide's story is truly like none other.
 
We are really hoping to gain more exposure for "Top Drawer", so again we would love to have you come out and review the show. 

We are now offering discounted student tickets for both Wednesday May 8th, and May 22nd for $10 at 7pm Theater 72 158 W 72nd street. Please spread the word by joining us on Facebook, and Twitter. For more details you can check us out at:
 
http://adelaidemestre.com/about/
https://www.facebook.com/mestreadelaide
http://www.womanaroundtown.com/sections/playing-around/top-drawer-coping-with-family-history

Best,
Daniel Lee Hue
Daniel@dmilesmedia.com
data.name: Come support "Top Drawer" Adelaide Mester

$10 Advance / $12 Door

Pittsburgh, PA 15222


About The Composure:
As a nod to some of the music that helped to shape their own sound, Pittsburgh pop-punkers THE COMPOSURE have announced “Singled Out”: A 90’s Covers Collection set for release on June 18.

Featuring hits from Semisonic, Fastball, Harvey Danger, Sublime, Blind Melon and Goo Goo Dolls, the digital EP will capture The Composure’s own power-pop essence within some of the biggest songs of the 90s. The band tracked the covers while in the studio with Jim Wirt (Jack’s Mannequin, Something Corporate, Incubus) at work on writing their follow-up to last spring’s EP Stay The Course.

Leading off with “Closing Time” – which premiered via video featurette at TheComposure.com today – the track list for Singled Out also includes “The Way” (featuring Jack O’Shea of Bayside), “Flagpole Sitta,” “Badfish,” “No Rain” and “Slide.”
